title: C Programming Fundamentals - Practice Exam Rubric

institution_context.target_students: FPT University students in foundational programming courses
course_context: Clear input-output format expected in academic lab assessments

easy.description: A short implementation task with straightforward input/output and one main concept.
expected_skills: Implement simple loops, conditions, arrays, or functions.
Produce correct output for small, direct requirements.
Follow a skeleton without needing deep debugging.

medium.description: An implementation task that requires combining multiple beginner concepts or handling several ordinary cases correctly.
expected_skills: Combine loops, arrays, functions, and validation logic.
Handle normal edge cases such as empty or boundary values.
should_avoid: Advanced memory management tasks outside course scope.

hard.description: A substantial beginner-to-intermediate C task requiring careful decomposition, edge-case coverage, and precise implementation.
expected_skills: Write a full solution with coherent hidden and visible test coverage.
should_avoid: Advanced data structure implementations unless clearly present in the chunks.

review_checks: The task must be grounded in the provided chunks.
The requested difficulty must match implementation complexity.
skeleton_code must match C language expectations.
solution_code must solve the stated task coherently.
test_cases must cover at least one visible case and should include hidden coverage.
The task must remain within introductory C scope.

easy: Requires multiple helper functions or several branching layers.
Needs broad edge-case handling beyond a direct introductory task.
medium: Is only a one-step syntax drill.
Requires advanced memory or pointer reasoning not supported by the source.
Has test coverage that implies a much harder hidden requirement than the statement suggests.
hard: Can be solved by a direct loop with no meaningful edge-case reasoning.
Has overly trivial visible and hidden tests.
Does not require decomposition or careful implementation choices.

clarity: The statement clearly says what the learner must read, compute, and print or return.
The task can be understood without seeing the original document.
pedagogical_value: The task checks an actual C programming skill, not only a memorized sentence from the chunk.
The task should help distinguish students who understand the concept from those who only guess.
non_triviality: Avoid pure copy-from-slide drills unless the chunk itself only supports a very small exercise.
Prefer a small but meaningful transformation, validation, or decision over a bare one-operator rewrite.
test_strength: Visible and hidden tests should check both the main behavior and at least one ordinary variation.
Tests should not all be near-duplicates with the same output pattern.

quality_red_flags: The statement is only a one-line syntax drill with no learner-facing context or behavioral framing.
The task simply paraphrases an example from the chunk without adding assessment value.
The tests are too weak to distinguish correct logic from lucky hardcoded output.
The title is generic and does not name the behavior being implemented.
quality_regeneration_hints: Make the PE task feel like a small lab exercise rather than a copied slide bullet.
Add a clearer behavior statement, a tiny realistic context, or a concrete requirement that still stays chunk-grounded.
Strengthen tests so they validate the intended logic instead of one lucky sample.

quality_exemplars.title_style: Check Whether a Student Score Is Pass or Fail
good_pattern: Uses a tiny real-world academic context.
Tests one main concept such as conditionals and input/output.
Makes the required output behavior explicit.
avoid_pattern: Only asks to use an operator without a learner-facing task.
Looks like a copied syntax bullet from lecture slides.

quality_exemplars.title_style: Compute the Largest of Three Integers
good_pattern: Combines direct input handling with short reasoning across multiple values.
Has tests that cover ordinary variation, not only one sample.
Still remains fully within beginner C scope.
avoid_pattern: Turns into a long multi-function design problem.
Adds hidden requirements not stated in the task.

question.title: Check Whether a Student Score Is Pass or Fail
question.description:
Write a C program that reads one integer score. If the score is at least 50, print PASS. Otherwise, print FAIL.

Input: one integer.
Output: PASS or FAIL on a single line.

question.title: Print the Largest of Three Integers
question.description:
Write a C program that reads three integers a, b, and c, then prints the largest value among them.

Input: three integers separated by spaces.
Output: the largest integer on a single line.

acceptance_rules: Accept only if the task statement, skeleton, solution, and tests are mutually consistent.
Reject if the solution does not logically match the problem statement.
Reject if hidden tests imply requirements not stated or grounded in the chunks.
regeneration_hints: Simplify the implementation scope for Easy tasks.
Add meaningful boundary cases for Medium and Hard tasks.
Keep the prompt aligned with beginner C learning outcomes.
